title: Image attestation and driver-safe deploy orchestration
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Goal: prevent shipment of container images that would fail or regress production when paired with reserved CUDA/driver permutations. Deliver an attestation + verification pipeline that binds image artifacts, SBOM deltas, and driver pinsets, and gates rollouts when attestation or compatibility checks fail.

Background: we frequently observe subtle regressions after image rollouts when the image's libraries or CUDA ABI expectations don't match the pinned driver matrix for Dedicated pools. Current SBOM collection is in place (SPDX), but there's no automated attestation tying SBOM/manifest to a driver-safelist nor a delta check that runs during canary promotion. This ticket implements:
  - Image attestation (cosign-based) + signing with KMS-backed keys
  - SBOM delta verification against known-good LTS cohorts (reject unexpected native libs that require newer drivers)
  - Driver-safe deploy orchestration: a pre-rollout gate that cross-checks image attestation + SBOM delta against the targeted Dedicated cohorts' driver matrix
  - Ops dashboard and alerting for blocked rollouts with suggested remediations.

Acceptance criteria:
  - Every image produced by CI has a cosign attestation signed by the release key and an SPDX SBOM artifact uploaded to the artifact registry.
  - Delta verifier can classify SBOM changes into: safe (source code/lib only), native-impacting (requires higher driver ABI), or unknown.
  - Rollout controller prevents promotion to Dedicated pools when the delta verifier reports "native-impacting" unless an escape hatch is taken with explicit approver (audit log required).
  - Integration tests that simulate CUDA ABI mismatch return non-zero and create a blocking ticket in the console.

Out of scope: making driver upgrades automatic; that will be a follow-up that implements scheduled driver cohort upgrades after compatibility validation.

2025-02-20 - Mateo A: PoC for cosign signing in CI is green on toy image. Created draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1543. Observed that musl-based images omit debug syms which makes delta classification harder; added step to extract native .so sonames.

2025-02-24 - Rajiv (platform): Ran SBOM delta classifier against LTS-2024-10 cohort. Classifier flagged libcuda.so version binary ABI change for 2 images. Filed follow-up ENG-41500 for test harness to produce reproducible ABI mismatch cases.

2025-02-27 - Security review (Elena): Requested formal threat model for signing key rotation and emergency rollback. Also asked for signed attestations to be verifiable offline (for Private customers). Added security_review_required=true.

2025-03-01 - Mateo A: Implemented initial rollout gate in canary controller. Gate consults: 1) attestation present and valid; 2) sbom-delta verdict != 'native-impacting' for the target cohort. Manual approver flow added for 'native-impacting' with 2 approvers required. Demo recorded: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/attestation-demo

2025-03-02 - QA (Li): Integration test failing intermittently when driver matrix contains multiple compatible driver revisions; unpinned drivers lead to false negatives. Working with infra to ensure the driver matrix is normalized by ABI level rather than exact driver string.

2025-03-03 - Aisha B: Decision log: Use SPDX v2.2 for SBOM exports; delta classifier will use soname and NEEDED entries plus a shallow symbol diff for high-confidence native-impacting detection. Next actions: finish PR review, add more integration test cases for CUDA 12.x vs 11.x ABI differences, and add console UI for blocked rollouts.
notes: This ticket touches both hosted and Dedicated pipelines. Private deployments will verify attestations but will manage signing keys on-prem; add ops checklist in follow-up. Coordinate with Compliance for auditable logs for the manual-approve escape hatch.
